nodes.label: NPC-R01

properties.statement: For transactions to be seamless, all stakeholders must consistently identify health products using standardized information.

nodes.note: Printed as the handbook's premise for product master data; a normative 'must' on all stakeholders.

evidence.quote: For transactions to be seamless, all stakeholders must consistently identify health products using standardized information.

nodes.label: NPC-R04

properties.statement: For effective use of data in operations, analysis, and decision-making, the integrity and quality of data must be consistently and continuously maintained.

nodes.note: The chapter's opening statement, without the running header the splitter joined to it.

evidence.quote: 16  Instituting data management and governance policies For effective use of data in operations, analysis, and decision-making, the integrity and quality of data must be consistently and continuously maintained.

nodes.label: NPC-R05

properties.statement: Data management policies should ensure adherence to principles of privacy, security, and ethical data usage.

nodes.note: A normative 'should' on data management policies.

evidence.quote: Data management policies should ensure adherence to principles of privacy, security, and ethical data usage.

nodes.label: NPC-R06

properties.statement: Master data management procedures should include the following key elements to continuously and securely maintain master data: • Data governance framework: Establish clear policies, roles, responsibilities, and processes to ensure data quality and consistency for use across the health supply chain.

nodes.note: The footnoted (*) statement on page 26, without the running header.

evidence.quote: Instituting data management and governance policies   17 *Master data management procedures should include the following key elements to continuously and securely maintain master data: • Data governance framework: Establish clear policies, roles, responsibilities, and processes to ensure data quality and consistency for use across the health supply chain.

nodes.label: NPC-R07

properties.statement: Data harmonization activities must consider all sources of product data, as well as the systems, processes, and organizations or stakeholders that will utilize this data.

nodes.note: A bullet of the step table on page 27.

evidence.quote: 18  Instituting data management and governance policies INPUTS STEPS RESOURCES OUTPUTS • Data harmonization activities plan • Master data management procedures including master data governance policies Conduct data harmonization activities such as establishing a standardized coding scheme, master data definitions and structures* to organize and maintain master data consistently and persistently • Data harmonization activities must consider all sources of product data, as well as the systems, processes, and organizations or stakeholders that will utilize this data.

nodes.label: NPC-R08

properties.statement: Master data definitions and structures should include provisions for maintaining product classifications, generic product information, and trade item details.

nodes.note: The footnoted (*) statement on page 28, without the running header.

evidence.quote: Instituting data management and governance policies   19 *Master data definitions and structures should include provisions for maintaining product classifications, generic product information, and trade item details.

nodes.label: NPC-R09

properties.statement: It is generally recommended to avoid including product classification or product characteristics such as dosage and strength in the generic national product code.

nodes.note: Printed under 'Best practices'; the figure caption before it is not part of it.

evidence.quote: 9: Relationship between generic product, trade item and regulated trade item Best practices: • It is generally recommended to avoid including product classification or product characteristics such as dosage and strength in the generic national product code.

nodes.label: NPC-R10

properties.statement: Instead, a system-generated sequential numeric or alphanumeric code should be used.

nodes.note: Best practice, first sentence of the bullet; the splitter joined the next bullet.

evidence.quote: Instead, a system-generated sequential numeric or alphanumeric code should be used. • Product characteristics such as dosage, strength, pack size, and route of administration should be defined as attributes and linked to the product codes.

nodes.label: NPC-R11

properties.statement: Product characteristics such as dosage, strength, pack size, and route of administration should be defined as attributes and linked to the product codes.

nodes.note: The next 'Best practices' bullet.

evidence.quote: Instead, a system-generated sequential numeric or alphanumeric code should be used. • Product characteristics such as dosage, strength, pack size, and route of administration should be defined as attributes and linked to the product codes.

nodes.label: NPC-R12

properties.statement: Generic national product codes, including drug codes and medicinal product identifiers (when using the WHO Drug Dictionary), should be mapped to trade item-specific identifiers, such as GTINs, or similar unique identifiers where GTINs are not available.

nodes.note: A 'Best practices' bullet.

evidence.quote: This combination of attributes and codes facilitates comprehensive identification of products. • Generic national product codes, including drug codes and medicinal product identifiers (when using the WHO Drug Dictionary), should be mapped to trade item-specific identifiers, such as GTINs, or similar unique identifiers where GTINs are not available. • The product coding system should maintain uniform code lengths and ensure scalability to accommodate an increasing number of unique products. • Product master data structures should support the mapping of one generic national product code to multiple corresponding trade items.

nodes.label: NPC-R13

properties.statement: The product coding system should maintain uniform code lengths and ensure scalability to accommodate an increasing number of unique products.

nodes.note: A 'Best practices' bullet.

evidence.quote: This combination of attributes and codes facilitates comprehensive identification of products. • Generic national product codes, including drug codes and medicinal product identifiers (when using the WHO Drug Dictionary), should be mapped to trade item-specific identifiers, such as GTINs, or similar unique identifiers where GTINs are not available. • The product coding system should maintain uniform code lengths and ensure scalability to accommodate an increasing number of unique products. • Product master data structures should support the mapping of one generic national product code to multiple corresponding trade items.

nodes.label: NPC-R14

properties.statement: Product master data structures should support the mapping of one generic national product code to multiple corresponding trade items.

nodes.note: A 'Best practices' bullet.

evidence.quote: This combination of attributes and codes facilitates comprehensive identification of products. • Generic national product codes, including drug codes and medicinal product identifiers (when using the WHO Drug Dictionary), should be mapped to trade item-specific identifiers, such as GTINs, or similar unique identifiers where GTINs are not available. • The product coding system should maintain uniform code lengths and ensure scalability to accommodate an increasing number of unique products. • Product master data structures should support the mapping of one generic national product code to multiple corresponding trade items.

nodes.label: NPC-R15

properties.statement: In addition, the data structure should organize multiple packaging levels and quantity relationships across those.

nodes.note: Continues NPC-R14's bullet; the remark after it explains why (packaging hierarchies are critical).

evidence.quote: In addition, the data structure should organize multiple packaging levels and quantity relationships across those. • Packaging hierarchies and quantity conversions across these levels—along with packaging variations among different brand items—are critical for countries to effectively manage supply chain operations such as inventory control and distribution.

nodes.label: NPC-R16

properties.statement: To address these concerns, procedures and systems should be developed to categorize data attributes based on their level of sensitivity.

nodes.note: A normative 'should' on data sensitivity categories.

evidence.quote: To address these concerns, procedures and systems should be developed to categorize data attributes based on their level of sensitivity.

nodes.label: NPC-R17

properties.statement: Access should then be controlled according to these sensitivity categories, ensuring appropriate data protection while enabling secure data sharing.

nodes.note: A normative 'should' on access control; follows NPC-R16.

evidence.quote: Access should then be controlled according to these sensitivity categories, ensuring appropriate data protection while enabling secure data sharing.

nodes.label: NPC-R18

properties.statement: The governance group should support the overall governance and planning of product master data standardization, capture, and dissemination activities, and provide leadership and oversight for all data management efforts.

nodes.note: A bullet of the step on establishing a master data governance group.

evidence.quote: Establish a master data governance group composed of all relevant stakeholders to provide leadership and guidance in managing product master data additions and changes. • The governance group should support the overall governance and planning of product master data standardization, capture, and dissemination activities, and provide leadership and oversight for all data management efforts. • The master data governance group can be integrated into existing governance structures or steering committees.

nodes.label: NPC-R19

properties.statement: When global identifiers such as GTINs are not available—e.g., if a manufacturer has not yet subscribed for a GTIN—it is recommended to use a local identifier for trade items.

nodes.note: Printed under 'Best practices'.

evidence.quote: Develop a change management plan to institutionalise use of NPC STEP 1 Best practices: When global identifiers such as GTINs are not available—e.g., if a manufacturer has not yet subscribed for a GTIN—it is recommended to use a local identifier for trade items.

nodes.label: NPC-R20

properties.statement: The plan should include: • Training of new users and newly hired staff involved in master data management • Encouraging participation in global and open standards conferences • Conducting advocacy sessions for operational users, emphasizing the benefits of standardized product master data.

nodes.note: The change-management plan's required contents.

evidence.quote: The plan should include: • Training of new users and newly hired staff involved in master data management • Encouraging participation in global and open standards conferences • Conducting advocacy sessions for operational users, emphasizing the benefits of standardized product master data.
